A static HMC transition requires a fixed number of leapfrog steps. The **No-U-Turn Sampler (NUTS)** chooses trajectory length during each transition. Hoffman and Gelman ([2014](https://jmlr.org/papers/v15/hoffman14a.html)) introduced the original algorithm; Stan uses a multinomial variant described in its [reference manual](https://mc-stan.org/docs/reference-manual/mcmc.html).

## Growing and stopping a trajectory

NUTS extends an HMC path forward or backward and organizes candidate states in a balanced binary tree. Increasing tree depth by one doubles the intended path length, though a turning condition or divergence may stop it early. The tree constructs one transition; its internal states are not additional posterior draws.

Let $q^-$ and $q^+$ be the trajectory endpoints and define

$$
\Delta q=q^+-q^-.
$$

An endpoint turning check examines

$$
\Delta q^\mathsf TM^{-1}\rho^-
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\Delta q^\mathsf TM^{-1}\rho^+.
$$

When one becomes negative, momentum at that endpoint points back across the path. Stan also checks completed subtrees. It selects one eligible state with weights related to $\exp\{-H(q,\rho)\}$, rather than automatically taking the final endpoint.

## Actual passage-level Student-t model tree lengths

The production passage-level Student-t fit used four chains, 750 warmup iterations, 1,000 retained iterations, `adapt_delta = 0.90`, and `max_treedepth = 10`. The code imports the original 55 passage summaries and the frozen draw object produced by the exact Stan program on the [next page](stan.qmd).

```{r}
#| label: load-provo-nuts-diagnostics
library(ggplot2)
library(posterior)

provo <- read.csv("data/provo/passage-summaries.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
y <- provo$noun_minus_verb_log_ffd
cache <- readRDS(
  "data/provo/provo-stan-draw-cache.rds"
)
diagnostics <- as.data.frame(as_draws_df(cache$production_diagnostics))

nuts_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(
  split(diagnostics, diagnostics$.chain),
  function(chain_data) data.frame(
    chain = chain_data$.chain[1],
    draws = nrow(chain_data),
    median_tree_depth = median(chain_data$treedepth__),
    maximum_tree_depth = max(chain_data$treedepth__),
    median_leapfrog_steps = median(chain_data$n_leapfrog__),
    maximum_leapfrog_steps = max(chain_data$n_leapfrog__),
    mean_acceptance_statistic = mean(chain_data$accept_stat__),
    divergences = sum(chain_data$divergent__)
  )
))

stopifnot(length(y) == 55L, nrow(diagnostics) == 4000L,
          sum(diagnostics$divergent__) == 0L,
          max(diagnostics$treedepth__) < 10L)
nuts_summary
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-provo-nuts-work
#| fig-cap: "Leapfrog work in the production passage-level Student-t fit. No transition reached the maximum tree depth."
work <- aggregate(n_leapfrog__ ~ .chain + treedepth__, diagnostics, length)
names(work)[3] <- "transitions"

ggplot(work, aes(treedepth__, transitions, group = factor(.chain),
                 color = factor(.chain))) +
  geom_line(linewidth = .65) +
  geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  scale_color_grey(start = .15, end = .7) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(work$treedepth__))) +
  labs(x = "Tree depth", y = "Transitions", color = "Chain") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

The maximum observed tree depth is `r max(diagnostics$treedepth__)`, and the maximum leapfrog count is `r max(diagnostics$n_leapfrog__)`. These are empirical properties of the production computation, not generic NUTS examples.

NUTS chooses trajectory length within a transition. Warmup adaptation separately learns the step size and mass matrix. Increasing `max_treedepth` only permits more work; it does not repair inaccurate integration, poor geometry, or weak identification.

## Check your understanding

1. What doubles when tree depth increases by one?
2. What sign indicates that an endpoint has turned back?
3. Why is only one state retained from a tree?
4. What does repeated maximum-depth saturation diagnose?

<details class="understanding-answers">
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. The intended number of leapfrog steps, and thus the path length, doubles. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
2. A negative endpoint dot product, $\Delta q^\mathsf T M^{-1}\rho^-<0$ or $\Delta q^\mathsf T M^{-1}\rho^+<0$, signals a turn back. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
3. The whole tree constructs one transition; retaining all internal states as draws would misrepresent their dependent selection mechanism. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
4. Repeated saturation indicates that the allowed trajectory length is truncating exploration, though it does not identify whether the cause is geometry, step size, or the depth cap. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->

</details>

The [Stan page](stan.qmd) shows the exact passage-level Student-t program and sampling call that generated these diagnostics.
